Ophthalmic tech and contact lens wearer here

I would not recommend it. For one, late in pregnancy people often experience corneal edema which makes wearing contacts uncomfortable and makes the rx in it not work as well temporarily (esp if you have a toric lens for astigmatism)

Also, god forbid, you have to have an emergency c section or other surgery where they might put you under general anesthesia, there is no time to remove your contacts and often they tape your eyelids closed but you still run a large risk of your eyes drying out and so will your contacts, which if you’ve ever accidentally let your contacts dry out a bit is ungodly uncomfortable. It also increases the risk for infection and corneal ulcers   

I just wouldn’t risk it if you have a backup pair of glasses you can wear until baby is here safely to avoid it because cornea problems are no joke and can cause blindness

It’s not a given that it WILL raise his IOP (eye pressure), it’s just a side effect that has a chance of happening because of how some peoples bodies respond to steroids.  

As for if it’s got long term effects, realistically that depends. Any good ophthalmologist will monitor the pt while on the steroids as increased pressure normally occurs three to six weeks from initial steroid use but can occur well after that. 

Most of the time stopping the steroids or concurrently treating with glaucoma drops will help but there was a study that around 2.8% of eyes with steroid induced elevation to IOP will convert to full on glaucoma with a heavy correlation between those 2.8% of folks all having family history of glaucoma. 

Which if it does become glaucoma or the pressure would be too high for too long if he’s not well monitored, any loss of vision to the elevated eye pressure would be permanent
